subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm planning proportions for the scene: a small red-eyed tree frog (~4-5cm) perched on a larger leaf (~20cm), working out how they sit together on the ground plane with the leaf near the base.

Now I'm sketching the frog's skeleton—hips, a spine chain built with catmull curves, head and jaw joints—then planning to sweep an elliptical cross-section along that spine for the body, with color sectors for the cream belly and blue flank markings.

Writing paint function...

Now I'm shaping the head and jaw geometry using scaled sphere parts positioned relative to the skull and jaw joint.

Now I'm placing bulging ruby-red eye spheres on the sides of the head, then adding small black slit pupils as flattened ellipsoids positioned on the eye's surface using directional offsets to orient them outward and slightly forward.

Writing SVG eye texture code...

I'll skip eyelids and mouth lines, keeping the expression simple with surprised eyes plus tiny nostril dots for detail. Now I'm sizing the decals relative to head proportions and planning the limb chain positions for the arms gripping the leaf.

Working through the limb bend directions and reach distances so each arm chain spans correctly from shoulder to hand.

Now I'm planning the toe structure for the feet—four digits with orange pads spread outward from the wrist/ankle point, fanning forward with small offset lengths for each toe chain.

Toes orange with pads a yellowish-orange, flattened spheres positioned at the tips sitting just above the leaf surface. Now I'm working out the hind leg fold: hip position, thigh angled up and back, shin forward, foot flat against the body.

For the two-segment hind limb, I'm computing knee displacement geometrically from hip to ankle target distance versus segment lengths, then figuring out the correct hint direction so the knee bulges outward and forward the way a real frog's bent leg would.

For the foot, I'm chaining a three-segment limb from ankle to toe tip, using a sole constraint so the last segment aligns exactly with the ground direction, and passing a single bend hint since the sole removes one degree of freedom.

Toes base attaches where the sole ends, keeping both at the same height so they sit flush. I'm tapering the thigh radius down the leg with a smooth array of values and picking lime for the thighs with orange feet, maybe adding stripe accents.

Adding blue belly-side sector...

Adjusting body position so the belly sits just above the leaf with a small clinging gap, lowering hips and spine y-values slightly and matching head and eye heights accordingly.

For the throat area I'm giving the jaw a lime tone with a cream patch underneath for the chin, and setting up the leaf as an extruded shape in the xz plane with a thin centered thickness.

Plotting the pointed leaf outline with smoothed corners, checking the point order to make sure it traces a clean counter-clockwise, non-self-intersecting path.

Now I'm painting the leaf with a midrib and side vein pattern using deep green tones against a lighter vein color, with a lime-colored frog for contrast against a darker leaf base, and adding a thin stem rod extending below the leaf.

I'm thinking through how the leaf should attach to the skeleton—likely riding on the nearest joint like hips since it's a rigid rest-pose element. Now I'm working out a toe-generation function that spreads digits outward and forward for the front hands using angular offsets and directional vectors.

Writing toe geometry...

Adding pad and toe spheres with distinct colors, then placing tiny nostril spheres on the snout surface and checking they align with the ellipsoid head shape at that position.

Now I'm positioning the eyes near the top of the head, sizing them with small spheres, and giving them a ruby-red tone while checking overall frog height stays reasonable.

I'm setting up the eye decal placement using azimuth angles so each eye faces outward laterally, then thinking about whether to add dorsal speckles or flank stripes via a paint function that checks surface normals to color the blue body with vertical cream stripes on the sides.

Now I'm defining the countershade transition from lime to cream with a soft blend, and writing the paint logic that applies cream-and-blue stripes on the flanks and hind legs based on normal direction and position, keeping the belly boundary soft while making the flank stripe edge sharper.

I realize the flank band and belly zone overlap where blue overrides cream incorrectly, so I'm tightening the band condition to apply only to the rear portion of the body using a z-position cutoff. Now I'm moving on to defining the head joint, attaching it to the spine with an explicit parent joint reference and setting its position and direction.

I'm also working out the jaw joint parented to the head, confirming the chain for the spine uses the body sweep with a radius function, and sorting out parent joints for the hind and front legs plus unique naming per side for the arms. For the limb chains, I'm deciding whether to use the points directly as angular polylines or smooth them with catmull interpolation for better bends.

Setting hip joint position for the spine base, choosing small sweep radii for the arms with low-poly sides, and placing shoulder joints so they sit just inside the body's edge. I'm also picking elbow hint directions for the arms and starting to define the hip position for the hind legs.
